standing_assumptions:
The work is a four-page note (Journal of Causal Inference, DOI 10.1515/jci-2016-0007) in an online-first layout: no page numbers are printed, so every location below is a PDF page. It contains one assumption, two definitions, four propositions and one corollary, all on PDF pp. 1-3; there is no appendix, supplement or code. Everything quoted below was read from the rendered page images.
[S1. Population and effects: Section 2, first paragraph, PDF p. 1] “Consider a full data probability distribution $G$ with an associated causal effect distribution $\tau$ with finite expectation $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, where $\mathrm{E}_G[.]$ denotes the expectation over the distribution $G$. Further denote the support of the distribution of $\tau$ as $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$. We impose a regularity condition on $\tau$ establishing non-degeneracy of $\tau$.”
[S2. Assumption 1: PDF p. 1] “Assumption 1: (Effect heterogeneity). $\min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right) = c > 0$.” Followed by: “Assumption 1 is equivalent to assuming that causal effects are not constant across observations in the distribution $G$; i.e., causal effects are heterogeneous.”
[S3. Data and estimator: PDF p. 1] “We do not observe the full data probability distribution $G$, but we observe an empirical distribution $F_n$. Suppose that, using $F_n$, we have a root-n consistent and asymptotically normal estimator of the average causal effect $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, $\hat\theta$.”
[S4. Definition 1: PDF p. 2] “Definition 1: An estimator $\hat\theta$ is root-n consistent and asymptotically normal for $\theta_0$ if $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0) = N(0, \sigma^2) + o_p(1)$, for some $0 < \sigma^2 < \infty$.”
[S5. Definition 2: PDF p. 2] “We now define the target parameter, $\theta_{F_n}$.” “Definition 2: Let the target parameter $$\theta_{F_n} = \begin{cases} \hat\theta & : |\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c \\ \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c & : \hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] > c \\ \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c & : \hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] < -c \end{cases},$$ where, as in Assumption 1, $c = \min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right)$.” Followed by: “The target parameter adapts naturally to the closest value in an interval surrounding $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, where the width of the interval is defined by the support of $\tau$. We formalize how each $\theta_{F_n}$ is a local average treatment effect.”
[Which hypotheses each printed result names] Proposition 1 names none (it inherits S1, S3 and Definition 2). Proposition 2 assumes only that $\hat\theta$ is root-n consistent and asymptotically normal for $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$; it does not name Assumption 1. Propositions 3 and 4 assume Assumption 1; Proposition 4 replaces Definition 1 by its own condition on $\hat\theta$. Corollary 1 names only its own support condition.
[What the paper does not print; the readings below are those of the audit’s validators, not the paper’s] (i) The sampling scheme that produces $F_n$ and the probability space on which $\hat\theta$ is defined are not specified (PDF p. 1 says only “we observe an empirical distribution $F_n$”). $\Pr$ and the unsubscripted $\mathrm{E}$ in Propositions 3-4 and Corollary 1 are read as the sampling distribution of $\hat\theta$ induced by $G$. The index $n$ on $\hat\theta$, $\tilde\theta$, $u$ and $\varepsilon$ is suppressed in the paper. (ii) “Support” is read as the closed support of the law of $\tau$; only its infimum $L$ and supremum $U$ (the essential infimum and supremum, possibly $-\infty$ and $+\infty$) enter. $c = +\infty$ is allowed (support unbounded in both directions), and then $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$. For $\tau$ with finite mean, Assumption 1 holds if and only if $\tau$ is not almost surely constant. (iii) Definition 2 says that $\theta_{F_n}$ is $\hat\theta$ clipped to $[\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c, \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c]$: with $\mu = \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$ and $C(x) = \min(\mu + c, \max(\mu - c, x))$, $\theta_{F_n} = C(\hat\theta)$; the targets also write $r(x) = x - C(x)$, so that $\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n} = r(\hat\theta)$. (iv) “Nonnegative weighting” (Proposition 1) is not defined; it is read as a measurable function $w \ge 0$ on the full-data population with $0 < \mathrm{E}_G[w] < \infty$ and $\mathrm{E}_G[|w\tau|] < \infty$, which may depend on every full-data variable and on the realized $F_n$. (v) The equation in Definition 1 is read as convergence in distribution of $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \theta_0)$ to $N(0, \sigma^2)$, or, in the form the printed proof of Proposition 3 uses, as $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \theta_0) = Z_n + R_n$ with $Z_n \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ and $R_n \to 0$ in probability. The witnesses in P017-T5, P017-T6 and P017-T12 satisfy the second form with an exactly normal $Z_n$; the witness in P017-T1 satisfies the first by the central limit theorem for independent, identically distributed, bounded summands. In Proposition 4, “$N(0, \sigma^2) + \varepsilon$” is read as $Z_n + \varepsilon_n$ with $Z_n \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ and no independence assumed between $Z_n$ and $\varepsilon_n$.
[Why the list has these targets] Four findings rated as errors concern a mathematical statement: P017-E001 (Moderate: Proposition 1 and the fact cited as its proof), P017-E002 (Moderate: steps in the printed proofs of Propositions 3 and 4), P017-E004 (Minor: the probability printed as 0 in the proof of Corollary 1, and the missing differential in the display of the proof of Proposition 4) and P017-N001 (Minor: the word “quickly” after Proposition 3, an overstatement that the validator settled with an exact counterexample). Each has a corrected-statement target, and a counterexample target where a validator gave one. Not targets: P017-E003 (rated a clarity note; its repair of the same sentence is quoted in P017-T13), P017-N002 (not confirmed), P017-N003 (bibliographic misprints), and headline claim P017-H6 (an interpretive remark in the Discussion). Headline claims H2, H1 and H4 are Propositions 1, 3 and 4, which findings P017-E001 and P017-E002 touch (P017-T9, P017-T14, P017-T15). H3 is Proposition 2 (P017-T16). The mathematical content of H5 is Corollary 1 (P017-T10) and the every-positive-sequence form of Proposition 3 (P017-T7).

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Display in the proof of Proposition 4: the normal tail integral, with its differential restored, and its closed form
canonical_claim.location: PDF p. 3 (no page number is printed)
canonical_claim.statement:
[Printed: the display in the proof of Proposition 4, PDF p. 3] $$\mathrm{E}_G[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] \le 2\int_c^\infty x^2 \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{x^2 n}{2\sigma^2}} = c\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\frac{e^{-\frac{c^2 n}{2\sigma^2}}}{\sqrt{n}} + 2\sigma^2\frac{\Phi\left(\frac{-c\sqrt{n}}{\sigma}\right)}{n} = o(n^{-1}).$$ No differential is printed in the integral.
[Correction. Sol’s smallest_repair for P017-E004 (validated.json), second sentence: “Append $dx$ to the first integral in the proof of Proposition 4.”]
Corrected identity in full. For every integer $n \ge 1$ and all real $c > 0$ and $\sigma > 0$, with $\Phi$ the standard normal distribution function, $$2\int_c^\infty x^2\,\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\,e^{-\frac{x^2 n}{2\sigma^2}}\,dx \;=\; c\,\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\,\frac{e^{-\frac{c^2 n}{2\sigma^2}}}{\sqrt{n}} \;+\; 2\sigma^2\,\frac{\Phi\left(\frac{-c\sqrt{n}}{\sigma}\right)}{n}.$$ Equivalently, with $s = \sigma/\sqrt{n}$, $a = c/s$ and $\phi$ the standard normal density: the left side is $\mathrm{E}[W^2\mathbf{1}\{|W| > c\}]$ for $W \sim N(0, s^2)$; $\int_a^\infty z^2\phi(z)\,dz = a\,\phi(a) + \Phi(-a)$; and both sides equal $2cs\,\phi(c/s) + 2s^2\,\Phi(-c/s)$.
Limit, as printed in the third line of the display: for fixed $c > 0$ and $\sigma > 0$ the common value is $o(n^{-1})$ as $n \to \infty$ (in fact $o(n^{-k})$ for every fixed $k > 0$).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: [$c$: Assumption 1, PDF p. 1] here any fixed positive real (for $c = +\infty$ the integral is over an empty range and equals $0$). [$\sigma$: Definition 1 and Proposition 4] $0 < \sigma^2 < \infty$. [$\Phi$: proof of Proposition 3, PDF p. 2] “$\Phi(.)$ denotes the standard Normal CDF”. [The integrand] $x^2$ times the density of $N(0, \sigma^2/n)$ at $x$, the law of $\tilde\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: The identity is exact for each $n$; it is the finite content. Steps (validator batch derivations.md, section P017-E004; derivation for P017-E002, section 6): substitute $x = sz$; integrate by parts using $\phi'(z) = -z\phi(z)$, which gives $\int_a^\infty z^2\phi(z)\,dz = [-z\phi(z)]_a^\infty + \int_a^\infty\phi(z)\,dz = a\phi(a) + \Phi(-a)$; and $2s^2a\phi(a) = c\sigma\sqrt{2/\pi}\,e^{-c^2n/(2\sigma^2)}/\sqrt{n}$. The limit clause is the only asymptotic statement: $n$ times the value is $c\sigma\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\sqrt{n}\,e^{-c^2n/(2\sigma^2)} + 2\sigma^2\Phi(-c\sqrt{n}/\sigma) \to 0$.
canonical_claim.note: The second misprint of P017-E004 (Minor): a normal integral printed without its differential. With $dx$ supplied, the printed evaluation is correct; the validator checked it by integration by parts and by quadrature at three parameter sets (work/checks.py, work/checks-output.json), and the fresh readers checked it symbolically. This target is the integral and its closed form only. The left-hand side of the printed display, $\mathrm{E}_G[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] \le \cdots$, is a different matter: that inequality is false for the Definition 2 target (P017-E002; P017-T6) and holds for the clip of $\tilde\theta$ (last display of P017-T8). The subscript $G$ on that expectation was raised and is not an error (verdict for P017-E004, part (c)). The rating records no headline claim as affected; the display belongs to the proof of Proposition 4 (P017-H4, P017-T15).

canonical_claim.definitions_needed: [Effect distribution, $\mathrm{E}_G$, $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$: Section 2, first paragraph, PDF p. 1] “a full data probability distribution $G$ with an associated causal effect distribution $\tau$ with finite expectation $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, where $\mathrm{E}_G[.]$ denotes the expectation over the distribution $G$”; “the support of the distribution of $\tau$ as $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$”. [$c$: Assumption 1, PDF p. 1, repeated in Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $c = \min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right)$; Assumption 1 is $c > 0$. [Target parameter: Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$ if $|\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] > c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] < -c$. [Root-n consistent and asymptotically normal: Definition 1, PDF p. 2] $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0) = N(0, \sigma^2) + o_p(1)$, for some $0 < \sigma^2 < \infty$ (readings in standing assumption (v)). [“quickly”] no rate is printed with the word; the validator reads it as implying rapid convergence of the probability of the event on which the estimator equals its target, and does not attribute a named bound to the sentence. [“inside the support of the effect distribution”] the intended event is $\{|\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c\}$ (finding P017-E003, a clarity note); in this witness the two events coincide, by (a) and (d). [Not in the paper; defined by the validator, derivation.md sections 2-4] the model, the fractional part $\{\cdot\}$, $W_n$, $B_n$, $A_n$, $p_n$ and the estimator; $\delta_{x}$ is the point mass at $x$. $B_n$ and $A_n$ are symmetric functions of the observed sample, so $\hat\theta_n$ is a function of $F_n$ and uses neither $\mu$ nor the unobserved effects.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: Parts (a), (b) and (d) are exact for every $n$. Proof of (b), validator derivation.md section 3: conditional on $U_2, \ldots, U_n$ with fractional part $t$ of their sum, the set of $u \in [0, 1)$ with $\{u + t\} < p_n$ has length $p_n$. In (c) the exact content for each $n$ is the inclusion $\{|\bar X_n| \le \tfrac12\} \cap \{B_n = 0\} \subseteq \{\varepsilon_n = 0\}$ and the bound $\Pr(|\bar X_n| > \tfrac12) \le 4/n$ (Chebyshev, $\mathrm{Var}(\bar X_n) = 1/n$). The limit statements are the last clauses of (c), (e) and (f).
canonical_claim.note: P017-N001 is rated an error, Minor (ratings.json); it is an overstatement in an explanatory sentence, and it is a target because the validator settled it with an exact counterexample (evidence_type: exact_counterexample; verdict confirmed_in_part; re-run upheld). Priority 3. What the witness shows: under Assumption 1 and Definition 1, even in the literal form “normal plus $o_p(1)$” with an exactly normal part, the probability of a nonzero estimation error can equal any prescribed sequence tending to zero. What it does not show: that Proposition 3 or Proposition 4 fails, or that the sentence prints a particular exponential bound (it does not; if “quickly” is read as purely rhetorical there is no rate claim to refute). The endpoint atoms of $V_i$ make every clipped target a weighted mean of effects (for $t \in [-1, 1]$ put weight $1 + t$ on $V = 1$ and $1 - t$ on $V = -1$), so the witness does not depend on the defect of P017-E001. The validator also shows that the estimator is root-n consistent and asymptotically normal for every $|\mu| < \tfrac12$, not only at $\mu = 0$ (derivation.md, section 4). All probabilities are exact rationals (check.py; no simulation); there is no Lean file in the artifact. The rating records no headline claim as affected; the merge step had listed the candidate as related to P017-H1 and P017-H5. The corrected claim is P017-T13.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Sentence after the proof of Proposition 3, as repaired (“quickly” deleted; the event is the interval of Definition 2)
canonical_claim.location: PDF p. 2 (no page number is printed)
canonical_claim.statement:
[Printed: PDF p. 2] “In short, Proposition 3 demonstrates that the probability that $\hat\theta$ falls inside the support of the effect distribution converges to one quickly; conditional on this event, then estimation error is zero (as the target parameter takes on the value as the estimator with probability one).”
[Correction. Sol’s smallest_repair for P017-N001 (validated.json), verbatim: “Delete 'quickly' from the first clause. For a precise formulation of the rate issue, say that the probability of lying in the clipping interval tends to one, without asserting a general rate.” The event is named by Sol’s repair of the same sentence under P017-E003 (a clarity note), verbatim: ‘Replace “inside the support of the effect distribution” by “inside the interval $[\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]-c,\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]+c]$”. On this event the estimator equals its target. Consistency makes the probability of this event tend to one.’]
Formal content of the corrected sentence. Let Assumption 1 hold ($c > 0$), let $\theta_{F_n}$ be as in Definition 2, write $\mu = \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, and let $\hat\theta_n$ be root-n consistent and asymptotically normal for $\mu$ (Definition 1). Then: (a) [exact, for every $n$] $\{|\hat\theta_n - \mu| \le c\} = \{\hat\theta_n = \theta_{F_n}\}$: on the event that $\hat\theta_n$ lies in $[\mu - c, \mu + c]$ the estimation error $\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n}$ is zero, and off that event it is not. (b) $\Pr(|\hat\theta_n - \mu| \le c) \to 1$ as $n \to \infty$. (c) No rate follows from these hypotheses: for every sequence $p_n \in (0, 1]$ with $p_n \to 0$ there exist a law $G$ satisfying Assumption 1 and an estimator satisfying Definition 1 such that $\Pr(|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > c) = \Pr(\hat\theta_n \ne \theta_{F_n}) = p_n$ for every $n \ge 1$ (the witness of P017-T12). (d) [a valid bound, exact for each $n$] if $\hat\theta_n = \tilde\theta_n + u_n$ with $\tilde\theta_n \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2/n)$, then $$\Pr\left(|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > c\right) \le 2\Phi\left(-\frac{c\sqrt{n}}{2\sigma}\right) + \Pr\left(|u_n| > c/2\right),$$ and the second term has no specified rate under $u_n = o_p(n^{-1/2})$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: [Effect distribution, $\mathrm{E}_G$, $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$: Section 2, first paragraph, PDF p. 1] “a full data probability distribution $G$ with an associated causal effect distribution $\tau$ with finite expectation $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, where $\mathrm{E}_G[.]$ denotes the expectation over the distribution $G$”; “the support of the distribution of $\tau$ as $\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]$”. [$c$: Assumption 1, PDF p. 1, repeated in Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $c = \min\left(\sup\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right) - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - \inf\left(\mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]\right)\right)$; Assumption 1 is $c > 0$. [Target parameter: Definition 2, PDF p. 2] $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$ if $|\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]| \le c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] > c$; $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c$ if $\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] < -c$. [Root-n consistent and asymptotically normal: Definition 1, PDF p. 2] $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_0) = N(0, \sigma^2) + o_p(1)$, for some $0 < \sigma^2 < \infty$ (readings in standing assumption (v)). [$\tilde\theta$, $u$, $\Phi$: proof of Proposition 3, PDF p. 2] $\hat\theta = \tilde\theta + u$ with $\tilde\theta = N(\mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \sigma^2/n)$ and $u = o_p(n^{-1/2})$; $\Phi$ the standard normal distribution function. [“Estimation error”] $\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n}$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (a) is exact [Definition 2: if $|\hat\theta - \mu| \le c$ then $\theta_{F_n} = \hat\theta$; otherwise $\theta_{F_n} = \mu \pm c \ne \hat\theta$]. (d) is exact for each $n$ [if $|\tilde\theta_n - \mu| \le c/2$ and $|u_n| \le c/2$ then $|\hat\theta_n - \mu| \le c$; union bound; $\Pr(|\tilde\theta_n - \mu| > c/2) = 2\Phi(-c\sqrt{n}/(2\sigma))$] (validator derivation.md, section 6). (b) rests on the consistency step: for each $n$ and each $M > 0$ with $c\sqrt{n} > M$, $\Pr(|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > c) \le \Pr(\sqrt{n}\,|\hat\theta_n - \mu| > M)$, together with $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_n - \mu) = O_p(1)$ from Definition 1. (c) is existential and is proved by the exact events of P017-T12(a)-(d).
canonical_claim.note: The corrected version of a Minor error (P017-N001); priority 3. The repair deletes one word and weakens only the explanatory clause (repair_cost: weaker_conclusion); it changes no assumption, estimand or stated result. The sentence must name the right event for (a) and (b) to be true, which is why Sol’s repair for P017-E003 is quoted: literal membership of $\hat\theta$ in the support of $\tau$ is neither necessary nor sufficient for zero error (for $\tau = \pm 1$ with equal probability and a normal estimator, $\Pr(\hat\theta \in \mathrm{Supp}_G[\tau]) = 0$ for every $n$ while $\Pr(|\hat\theta| \le 1) \to 1$; validator batch derivations.md, section P017-E003). P017-E003 itself is rated a clarity note and has no target of its own. Part (c) is the precise sense of “without asserting a general rate”; part (d) is the validator’s statement of what can be said about the rate. A rate does follow under further tail control of $u_n$, for example under the mean-square condition of Proposition 4.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Proposition 3, with its proof as printed
canonical_claim.location: PDF p. 2 (no page number is printed)
canonical_claim.statement:
[PDF p. 2] “We now turn to our primary result, proving the superefficiency of $\hat\theta$ in estimating $\theta_{F_n}$.” “Proposition 3: Suppose that Assumption 1 holds and that $\hat\theta$ is a root-n consistent and asymptotically normal estimator of $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$. Then $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n}) = o_p(1)$.”
[Proof as printed: PDF p. 2] “Proof: Decompose $\hat\theta$ into $\tilde\theta = N(\mathrm{E}_G[\tau], \sigma^2/n)$ and $u = o_p(n^{-1/2})$, so that $\hat\theta = \tilde\theta + u$. Since $(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})$ is $o_p(a_n)$ for any positive sequence $(a_n)$, the rate of convergence of $\hat\theta$ is at worst governed by the bound ensured by $u$’s $o_p(n^{-1/2})$ convergence. To prove the claim, note that for any positive $\varepsilon$, $\Pr\left(\frac{|\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n}|}{a_n} \ge \varepsilon\right) \le \Pr\left(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n} \ne 0\right) = 2\Phi(-c\sqrt{n}/\sigma)$, where $\Phi(.)$ denotes the standard Normal CDF. Since $\lim_{n\to\infty} 2\Phi(-c\sqrt{n}/\sigma) = 0$, $(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})$ is $o_p(a_n)$. Thus $\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n} = o_p(a_n) + o_p(n^{-1/2}) = o_p(n^{-1/2})$, yielding the result.”

canonical_claim.statement:
[PDF p. 2, last paragraph] “Our results can be generalized to stronger claims straightforwardly. When a regularity condition is imposed on the rate of convergence of $\hat\theta$ to normality, a stronger result can be obtained about the rate of mean square convergence.”
[PDF p. 3] “Proposition 4: Suppose that Assumption 1 holds and $\hat\theta$ obeys $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta - \mathrm{E}_G[\tau]) = N(0, \sigma^2) + \varepsilon$, where $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon^2] = o(n^{-1/2})$. Then $\mathrm{E}[(\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] = o(n^{-1})$.”
[Proof as printed: PDF p. 3] “Proof: We will show that the mean square error of $(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})$ converges to zero sufficiently quickly, implying that the rate of convergence of $\hat\theta$ is at worst governed by the mean square error bound ensured by $\varepsilon$’s convergence rate. To obtain the rate of convergence of the mean square error of $\tilde\theta$, we integrate over its squared deviation from the target parameter. Within $c$ of $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, the squared deviation is zero, thus we need only integrate over the squared deviation over the tails of the normal distribution. To ease calculations, we obtain an upper bound by integrating over the squared deviation from $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, rather than from $\theta_{F_n}$: $$\mathrm{E}_G[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] \le 2\int_c^\infty x^2 \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{x^2 n}{2\sigma^2}} = c\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\frac{e^{-\frac{c^2 n}{2\sigma^2}}}{\sqrt{n}} + 2\sigma^2\frac{\Phi\left(\frac{-c\sqrt{n}}{\sigma}\right)}{n} = o(n^{-1}).$$ Since $\mathrm{E}[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] = o(n^{-1})$ and $n^{-1/2}\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon^2] = o(n^{-1})$, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ensures that $\mathrm{E}[(\hat\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] = o(n^{-1}) + o(n^{-1}) = o(n^{-1})$.”

canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: Finite facts on which a valid proof rests (P017-T8; not printed): with $C$ the clip to $[\mathrm{E}_G[\tau] - c, \mathrm{E}_G[\tau] + c]$ and $r(x) = x - C(x)$, for every $n$: (1) $|r(x) - r(y)| \le |x - y|$; (2) $\mathrm{E}[(\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n})^2] \le 2\,\mathrm{E}[r(\tilde\theta_n)^2] + 2\,\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2]/n$; (3) $\mathrm{E}[r(\tilde\theta_n)^2] \le 3\sigma^4/(c^2n^2)$, and also $\mathrm{E}[r(\tilde\theta_n)^2] \le 2\int_c^\infty x^2 \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-\frac{x^2 n}{2\sigma^2}}\,dx$. Finite steps of the printed proof: (i) “Within $c$ of $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, the squared deviation is zero” and the first inequality of the display, both false for the target of Definition 2 (P017-T6); (ii) the closed form of the integral, correct once $dx$ is supplied (P017-T11); (iii) the last sentence: exactly, with $A = \tilde\theta_n - \theta_{F_n}$, $\mathrm{E}[(\hat\theta_n - \theta_{F_n})^2] = \mathrm{E}[A^2] + 2\,\mathrm{E}[A\varepsilon_n]/\sqrt{n} + \mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2]/n \le \left(\sqrt{\mathrm{E}[A^2]} + \sqrt{\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2]/n}\right)^2$ by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, and $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2]/n \le n^{-1/2}\,\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon_n^2]$ for $n \ge 1$, so this step is valid as printed (validator batch derivations.md, section P017-N002).
canonical_claim.note: Headline claim P017-H4; an asymptotic statement, hence priority 4. It is listed as touched by P017-E002 (Moderate): the proposition is true as stated under its printed assumptions (the fresh readers and the validator prove it by the Lipschitz argument of P017-T8, without independence of the normal part and the remainder); what fails is the printed proof, in the sentence “Within $c$ of $\mathrm{E}_G[\tau]$, the squared deviation is zero” and in the first inequality of the display (counterexample P017-T6). The intermediate conclusion $\mathrm{E}[(\tilde\theta - \theta_{F_n})^2] = o(n^{-1})$ is true for a different reason (P017-T8(e)). The Lean statement should be the proposition, not the printed proof steps. Two further candidates concern this proof: P017-E004 (the missing $dx$; corrected in P017-T11) and P017-N002 (the term $n^{-1/2}\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon^2]$ in the last sentence), which was not confirmed: the printed bound is true and sufficient, although $\mathrm{E}[\varepsilon^2]/n$ is the exact scale. The paper does not state whether $c = +\infty$ is intended; in that case the left side is identically zero.
